detailed_description: The SQL Formatter reformats SQL text to make queries easier to read, and can also minify SQL by removing extra whitespace. Paste a query, click Format for indentation and line breaks, or click Minify for compact output. It is useful for reviewing SELECT statements, cleaning copied snippets, and preparing examples for documentation. The tool formats text only; it does not connect to a database, execute SQL, validate schema names, or optimize query performance.
usage_steps: Paste SQL into the input editor.
Click Format to add readable spacing and line breaks.
Click Minify if you need compact SQL text.
Review the output for your database dialect.
Copy the result when it matches your style needs.
Test important queries in your own database environment.
usage_examples: Format a long SELECT query before code review.
Minify a SQL snippet for an environment variable.
Clean copied SQL before adding it to documentation.
Make a WHERE clause easier to inspect.

faqs.question: Does it execute SQL?
faqs.answer: No. It only formats or minifies SQL text in the page.

faqs.question: Does it optimize queries?
faqs.answer: No. It changes readability, not database execution plans.

faqs.question: Will every SQL dialect format perfectly?
faqs.answer: Dialect-specific syntax may need manual review after formatting.

faqs.question: Can it minify SQL?
faqs.answer: Yes. The page includes a minify action.

faqs.question: Does it upload my query?
faqs.answer: The visible formatting runs in the browser page and does not require account login.
